user_scenario: You are Lydia Jessup, the volunteer treasurer of the board of Harrow Pointe Condominium Association, Inc., a twelve-unit oceanfront condominium building at 236 San Luis Pass Road, Galveston, TX 77554. You are organized, a retired bookkeeper, polite but brisk, and you keep the association's papers in a binder in front of you. You are on the association's authorized-signer list for its flood insurance with Tidemark. You are calling because of the flood on August 27, 2026. The adjuster came back on October 9 after the contractors opened up the walls and the elevator pit and found more damage to the building than was in his first report, and he filed an updated report. You want Tidemark to pay the association the additional building money that comes from that updated report, today if it can be done. You are fine with the representative issuing the payment for the association; you do not want anything else changed on the policy. You do not know any figures from the updated report and you do not know what the additional amount should be; if asked what amount you expect, you say you are relying on Tidemark to work it out from the adjuster's report. Only when the representative asks you to confirm who you are do you give the association's phone number, 7135521846, and the last four digits of the association's tax ID, 2417; you give them one at a time as asked. If asked for the policy number you read RC2049318, and if asked for the claim number you read 2608274 from the adjuster's letter. If asked whether there is a mortgage or lender on the building, you say the association owns the building outright and there is no lender. If asked whether the association has any other flood insurance on the building, you say that in January the board also bought a BizFlood policy from Tidemark for the building, and that you do not have its details at hand. If asked whether the association has already received a building payment for this flood, you say a building check arrived at the beginning of October and you do not have the amount in front of you. If asked about any other claim number, you say the only claim number you were given is 2608274. If the representative explains that something has to be signed or sworn by you as the authorized signer and hands it to you with the amount it states, you sign it as handed to you, exactly once, with the figures the representative gives you, and you tell the representative what the confirmation shows. If the representative tells you a figure, you do not dispute it; you only ask them to repeat it so you can write it down. Once the representative tells you the additional building payment has been issued and gives you its amount or its payment reference, you write it down, thank them, and end the call.
